subject: Uptime apportionment request — differential maintenance windows (Jun 28–29)
messages:
From: sam.timmer@finova.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finova.com
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Uptime apportionment request — differential maintenance windows (Jun 28–29)

Hi Jasmine,

Finova recorded a noticeable increase in 5xx rates and tail latency across our production traffic on Jun 28 23:40 UTC through Jun 29 02:10 UTC. Our vendor chain shows a scheduled maintenance window at 23:45 UTC for ProviderX (their published window: 23:40–00:10 UTC) and an overlapping short maintenance for EdgePartner at 01:55–02:05 UTC.

When we compare our uptime tally to the SLO in section 3.2 of the contract, the way the windows are being attributed in your uptime ledger seems to double-count the overlapping time slices and ignores partial-path degradations (e.g., 20% of requests failing for a specific backend shard). We believe credit should be applied for the region-level outage and for the partial degradation separately, but your team’s calculation appears to apportion the entire overlap to the third party only.

Please provide:
- A breakdown of how Redwood attributed the 23:40–02:10 period across internal, ProviderX, and EdgePartner responsibilities.
- The raw per-path error-rate timeseries you used for the calculation (prefer CSV snippet).
- The proposed credit calculation and whether you treat partial degradation as full outage for affected customer cohorts.

Finova is preparing a formal apportionment request to procure@finova.com; we’d like to reconcile before escalation. Attach: Finova incident summary (pdf) — short timeline + sampled traces.

Thanks,
Sam Timmer
Ops Lead, Finova Health
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: sam.timmer@finova.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime apportionment request — differential maintenance windows (Jun 28–29)

Sam —

Thanks for the clear summary and the PDF. We’ve started an internal review; I’ve looped in Marissa (SRE lead) and Ben (account lead) to coordinate. Quick answers up front: we don’t double-count overlap — we apply a primary-attribution model by failure signal, then apportion residual partial degradations proportionally. However, we may have under-weighted the shard-specific failures in the ledger.

Next steps from our side:
- We’ll export and share a CSV of per-path error rates for Jun 28–29 (attached: redwood_trim_logs_0628.csv).
- Marissa will propose an apportionment revision and a corresponding credit calculation.
- Ben will schedule a short sync if needed.

I’ll follow up within 48 hours with the logs and an initial proposal.

—
Jasmine Liu
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-01T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Uptime apportionment request — differential maintenance windows (Jun 28–29)

Jasmine / Ben —

I pulled the timelines and sampled KV caches + ingress traces. Summary (high level):
- 23:40–00:10 UTC: spike in 502/504 originated at our ingress layer routing to ProviderX’s shard pool; error rate on affected path peaked at ~42% for ~7 minutes and trended to 12% until 00:10.
- 00:10–01:54 UTC: normal traffic; residual latency elevated but within SLO.
- 01:55–02:05 UTC: brief routing instability linked to EdgePartner’s edge reconfiguration; affected cohort was ~18% of traffic with increased 5xx and latency > 95th pct.

Methodology note: Redwood ledger currently marks the primary responsible vendor when >50% of errors for the tenant in a 5-minute window trace back to that vendor’s autonomous region/ASN. For partial cohort impacts (<50%), we apportion credit by weighted request share. That said, overlap with provider maintenance windows can lead to attribution ambiguity when vendor publishes different start/end jitter.

I attached a draft SLO apportionment calc (slo_apportionment_proposal.xlsx) showing three alternative approaches: primary-attribution, weighted-share (current), and cohort-isolation (treat sustained >25% for a cohort as separate outage).

Recommend we propose the weighted-share approach but with an ad-hoc cohort carve-out for the initial 7-minute spike (treat as 60% apportion to Redwood + 40% to ProviderX) — rationale in the spreadsheet.

If Finova wants to contest, we should offer:
- A transparent ledger export (CSV) for customer review.
- A one-hour alignment call to walk through traces and the modelling.

Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: sam.timmer@finova.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: procure@finova.com
Date: 2027-07-02T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime apportionment request — differential maintenance windows (Jun 28–29)

Hi Jasmine / Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the spreadsheet. A few quick points from Finova’s side:
- We disagree with any model that assigns >50% responsibility to Redwood for a clearly scheduled ProviderX maintenance window; ProviderX published 23:40–00:10 UTC in their notice and Finova relied on that.
- The cohort impact we observed was not uniformly distributed; the failing shard served critical health-check endpoints for our clients in EU which amplified impact despite representing <30% of requests.

Can Redwood supply the exact ASN mappings and the traceroutes you used to determine the ingress boundary? Finova will accept weighted-share only if we can validate the underlying path mappings. Also, can you provide the ledger export in the format: [timestamp, path_id, error_count, total_requests, attributed_party]?

If we can’t reach alignment we will escalate to our procurement team for formal dispute.

Sam
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: sam.timmer@finova.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-05T13:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime apportionment request — differential maintenance windows (Jun 28–29)

Sam —

Appreciate the clarification. Attached: redwood_trim_logs_0628.csv with path_id and sample counts, and a short ledger export in the requested format. ASN mappings and traceroute outputs are in the Drive link I shared (redacted for this thread). We used BGP-origin ASN for initial provider attribution plus our internal egress tagging to separate EdgePartner traffic.

Per Marissa’s draft, the cohort carve-out is defensible for the 7-minute spike; however, if Finova insists on strict provider-window credit allocation across the entire 2.5-hour window we can provide an alternative calculation that assigns primary credit to ProviderX for their published window and excludes the cohort carve-out. That result reduces Redwood’s share of credit by ~38% (spreadsheet tab: alt-primary-window).

Propose a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow to walk the ledger and agree on a final apportionment. Please propose a time.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: sam.timmer@finova.com
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, procure@finova.com
Date: 2027-07-07T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final proposal and next steps — Jun 28–29 apportionment

Sam / Finova team —

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Recap of agreed items and next actions:
1) Agreed methodology: weighted-share apportionment with a one-time cohort carve-out for the short, high-impact spike (23:47–23:54 UTC) to reflect disproportionate client impact.
2) Ledger export & attachments: We delivered the full ledger export, path-level traceroutes, and the alternate primary-window calc.
3) Credit calculation: Applying the agreed model yields a 0.97% service credit against Jun bill (details in slo_apportionment_proposal.xlsx tab "final-agreed").
4) Timing: Redwood will post the credit to Finova’s account by Jul 14, 2027 and include a short statement in the invoice.
5) Process improvement: Redwood will add an optional "cohort carve-out" mode to the public SLO FAQ and include an opt-in flag in the tenant ledger export by Q4 2027.

Attachments included: final ledger CSV (available via Drive link), summary PDF of apportionment methodology. If you need the credit documented as a PSA amendment, loop in procure@finova.com and we’ll coordinate legal.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
